vignette:
Raj, a 49-year-old military medic, sits across from his therapist, his hands resting in his lap, fingers intertwined as if they are trying to hold him together. He has always been the one to provide care, tending to soldiers on the battlefield, patching them up and reassuring them. But today, as he shares his story, it's clear that Raj needs healing himself.

The trauma began several years ago, during a deployment in a war zone. While Raj was accustomed to the chaos and unpredictability of military life, nothing prepared him for the emotional turmoil that would follow. He recalls the day vividly: the sun was setting, casting long shadows across the sand, when he received a call from his wife, Priya. Her voice trembled as she explained the situation-her brother had been drinking, and it escalated into a violent confrontation. Raj's heart raced; he felt helpless, torn between duty and the instinct to protect his loved ones. 

Despite the distance, Raj's mind races with guilt and anger as he thinks about that night. He had been able to save countless lives on the front lines, yet he was unable to save Priya from her brother's fists. The helplessness gnaws at him, even now. He recalls returning home weeks later to find Priya changed. She was quieter, her laughter replaced with a distant gaze. The physical signs of the violence weren't as evident, but Raj sensed the emotional scars etched deeply within her. 

As the weeks turned into months, Raj began to notice the aftermath of that night creeping into his life. At work, he finds himself hyper-vigilant, twitching at every loud noise, jumping at the sound of a door slamming. Where once he had thrived in the fast-paced environment of the medical tent, now he struggles to concentrate, his mind often drifting back to Priya, to the fear that gripped him when he received that call. He can still hear her voice, a mix of fear and urgency, echoing in his mind. 

At home, Raj tries to be strong for Priya, but the weight of his own trauma hangs heavily on his shoulders. He feels as though he is living in two different worlds-one where he dons his uniform and plays the role of the strong protector, and another where he fights his own demons in silence. He often finds himself staring blankly at the TV, unable to engage with the shows that once brought him joy. Instead, his mind spirals into a cycle of "what ifs" and "should haves." 

The intimacy between him and Priya suffers. Their once vibrant relationship has become a series of strained conversations and awkward silences. Raj feels a growing chasm between them, fueled by his inability to express what he has been through. He fears that if he opens up about his own pain, it will only add to Priya's suffering. So, he keeps his feelings bottled up, leading to moments of anger that he later regrets. He finds himself snapping at small things-missing the salt container or forgetting to take out the trash-when in reality, it is the unresolved trauma that triggers the outbursts.

Raj's nightmares become a nightly occurrence. He dreams of the battlefield, but instead of his comrades, he sees Priya's brother, his face twisted in rage. He wakes up drenched in sweat, heart pounding, unable to shake the feeling of dread that lingers long after the dream fades. The exhaustion seeps into his work, and he begins to worry about the effects of his mental state on his performance. The thought of failing his comrades terrifies him, making him push through the pain, even as he feels himself slipping.

In therapy, Raj often speaks of the conflicting emotions he navigates daily. He feels an overwhelming sense of responsibility to protect those around him, yet he struggles with his own vulnerability. He wonders why he can't apply the same resilience that he shows in his medical practice to his personal life. As he shares these thoughts, he realizes he is not just a medic; he is also a survivor, grappling with the shadows of his past while trying to reclaim his present. 

Raj's journey is one of navigating the complex web of trauma, guilt, and love, as he seeks to find a way to heal not only for himself but for Priya too. Each session, he slowly uncovers pieces of himself that he thought were lost forever, hoping to rebuild the man he once was while forging a new path forward.
